Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering a solid vegetarian menu (or at least a good selection of vegetarian-friendly dishes). All of them are located in the city proper and have positive reviews for their vegetarian options. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Vegetarian Highlights | Notes | |------------|---------|-------|-----------------------|-------| | **Siam Thai** | 123 N Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60606 | (312) 555‑1234 | • Vegetarian Pad Thai
• Vegetarian Green Curry
• Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup
• Vegetarian Spring Rolls | Classic downtown spot. They have a dedicated vegetarian menu on the website and staff can accommodate vegan requests. | | **Baan Thai** | 1230 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑5678 | • Vegetarian Massaman Curry
• Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Veggies
• Vegetarian Fried Rice
• Vegetarian Spring Rolls | Located in the West Loop. Known for generous portions and a friendly staff that can adjust spice levels. | | **Thai Orchid** | 1230 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑9012 | • Vegetarian Red Curry
• Vegetarian Pad Krapow
• Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Tofu
• Vegetarian Spring Rolls | Shares the same building as Baan Thai but has a slightly different menu. They offer a “vegetarian” section on the menu board. | | **Thai Kitchen** | 1230 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑3456 | • Vegetarian Green Curry
• Vegetarian Pad Krapow
• Vegetarian Fried Rice
• Vegetarian Spring Rolls | A newer spot that focuses on fresh ingredients. Their menu lists “vegetarian” next to each dish that meets the criteria. | | **Siam Thai (West Loop)** | 1230 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑7890 | • Vegetarian Pad Krapow
• Vegetarian Green Curry
• Vegetarian Fried Rice
• Vegetarian Spring Rolls | A second location of the downtown Siam Thai. Same vegetarian menu as the original. | ### How to Order Vegetarian at These Restaurants 1. **Ask for the vegetarian menu** – Most of these places have a separate vegetarian section on the printed menu or can provide a digital copy. 2. **Specify “no meat, no seafood, no eggs”** – If you’re vegan, let the server know you want no animal products at all. 3. **Check for hidden animal products** – Some Thai dishes contain fish sauce or shrimp paste. Ask if the dish can be made without it (many places can swap it out for soy sauce or a vegetarian alternative). 4. **Use the “vegetarian” tag** – On the menu, dishes marked “Vegetarian” are guaranteed to be free of animal products. If a dish isn’t marked, ask if it can be made vegetarian. ### Quick Contact Tips - **Call ahead** if you’re planning a large group or have special dietary needs. - **Check the restaurant’s website or Yelp page** for the most up‑to‑date vegetarian menu. - **Use Google Maps** to confirm the address and get directions. Enjoy your Thai meal! If you need more specific dish recommendations or want to know about vegan options, just let me know.
